newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Perdigao sees $1.2 bln '97 sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Perdigao sees $1.2 bln '97 sales.

text.p: Brazilian meat processor Perdigao foresees a 19-percent jump in sales value next year to $1.2 billion as efficiency, prices and sales volume improve, the company's president said.
"We expect to raise sales of all our products," Perdigao chief Nildemar Secches told Reuters in an interview.
Perdigao, Brazil's number two meat producer, expects to post sales this year totalling $1 billion, up from $936 million in 1995 despite a decline in prices, he said.
"In volume, we had a good year this year but prices fell a little," Secches said.
Exports to Asia, Europe and the Middle East are expected to total some $300 million in 1997, compared with a projected $240 million in overseas sales this year.
Secches said the company expects to boost exports to Germany next and also enter the Argentine and Paraguayan markets as it seeks to expand its presence in the four-nation Mercosur customs union.
"We're going to have a sales base in Argentina and Paraguay," he said, adding the firm expects to sell mostly ham, salami, sausages and other swine derivatives in the neighbouring countries.

Perdigao, which already exports to Mercosur partner Uruguay, will not have to modify products for Paraguay's market but will need to alter taste and color on some products for Argentine consumers, he added.
The Perdigao line should hit Argentine and Paraguayan markets in 60 to 90 days, he added.
Meanwhile, the firm in 1997 expects to invest some $100 million, including $80 million on a project to boost efficiency at its southern Brazil plant.
The firm also expects by 2003 to spend a total of $275 million on its new Rio Verde plant in Goias state, which will double the firm's output capacity, and $30 million on a new Minas Gerais plant.
"We plan to start production at both facilities by mid-1999 and expect to complete construction by 2003," Secches said.
Despite the ambitious investment plans, Perdigao is not in immediate need of external financing.
With some $250 million in cash on hand, the firm does not plan to launch American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) or debt on global markets in 1997.
He said Perdigao, which already trades a Level One ADR in the United States, is studying the possible launch of Level Two or Three ADRs.
But he added: "We don't have any plans in the short-term."
